text: By Noether's theorem, the time-translation symmetry of a system's laws (the laws being the same today as yesterday) corresponds to the conservation of which quantity?
explanation: Noether's theorem pairs each continuous symmetry with a conserved quantity, and time-translation symmetry yields conservation of energy. Linear momentum corresponds instead to spatial-translation symmetry and angular momentum to rotational symmetry, so options 0 and 1 name the wrong symmetry; electric-charge conservation follows from an internal gauge symmetry rather than a spacetime symmetry.
